hook.line: Everyone has a theory about Altamira. Hernando gives his over a tinto and Mariana gives hers in print. They are both guessing, but one is a hunch and the other keeps the door open, and Spanish makes you pick the right frame.
hook.es: Para mí que Altamira ya compró el edificio.
hook.en: If you ask me, Altamira has already bought the building.

examples.en: If you ask me, he's not coming.

rule:
Both frames guess, but they guess differently.

*Para mí que* is a hunch, said over coffee. You lean one way, so the verb is plain: *Para mí que no viene.* It is the mood of "I'd bet".

*Cabe la posibilidad de que* is formal. You hold the idea open without leaning, so the verb takes the wish form: *Cabe la posibilidad de que no venga.* It suits a report or a meeting.

So ask two things: do I lean, and who am I talking to? A friend and a lean: *para mí que*. A room and an open door: *cabe la posibilidad de que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the indicative after an opinion marker versus the subjunctive after an expression of possibility.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *viene* or *venga* and type the whole sentence, as a hunch: *Para mí que no ___.*
yourTurn.why: A hunch with *para mí que* keeps the plain verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *viene* or *venga* and type the whole sentence, formally: *Cabe la posibilidad de que no ___.*
yourTurn.answer: Cabe la posibilidad de que no venga.
yourTurn.why: After *cabe la posibilidad de que*, the verb takes the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: If you ask me, Altamira has already bought the building.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que Altamira ya compró el edificio.
yourTurn.why: It is a hunch, so the verb stays plain.

yourTurn.prompt: Say formally: There's a possibility that Altamira will buy the building.
yourTurn.answer: Cabe la posibilidad de que Altamira compre el edificio.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: If you ask me, the mayor knows more than he says.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que el alcalde sabe más de lo que dice.
yourTurn.why: *Para mí que* plus *sabe*: you lean this way.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal: *Para mí que Tomás se queda.* (There's a possibility that Tomás will stay.)
yourTurn.answer: Cabe la posibilidad de que Tomás se quede.
yourTurn.why: Moving from hunch to open possibility changes the frame and the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a hunch, negative: *Para mí que hay trato.* (If you ask me, there's no deal.)
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que no hay trato.
yourTurn.why: *No* goes in front of the verb; the verb stays plain.

pitfalls.why: Almost. A hunch leans one way, so use the plain verb, not the wish form.

pitfalls.wrong: Cabe la posibilidad de que no viene.
pitfalls.right: Cabe la posibilidad de que no venga.
pitfalls.why: This frame holds the idea open, so the verb takes the wish form.

pitfalls.wrong: Cabe la posibilidad que no venga.
pitfalls.right: Cabe la posibilidad de que no venga.

personal: Give your theory about something small, like whether the bakery will open on time. First as a hunch with *Para mí que...*, then formally with *Cabe la posibilidad de que...*.
